什么时候需要把图片转成 PDF

JPG / PNG 是「图片」，PDF 是「文档」。接收方要的是一份固定版式的文件时，就该转 PDF：

  • 证件与材料提交：政务、银行、学校、签证系统几乎只收 PDF——多张证件照按顺序合成一个文件，一次传完。
  • 合同 / 单据回传：拍照或扫描后的签字页合成 PDF 回传，页序固定、对方无法轻易改动单页。
  • 多图打包发送：十几张截图发给对方，不如一个 PDF——接收方按页翻看，顺序不会乱，也不会被聊天工具二次压缩。
  • 打印：把图片放进 A4 页面再打印，比直接打印图片更可控（页边距、居中、缩放都固定了）。

反过来，如果对方要的是「继续编辑的素材」，请保留原始图片格式，别转 PDF。

页面尺寸：适配图片 vs A4 / Letter

选项页面大小适合场景
适配图片每页正好一张原图屏幕阅读：邮件附件、聊天发送、在线提交预览
A4210×297mm（595×842pt）国内/欧洲的打印与正式提交
Letter216×279mm（612×792pt）北美地区的打印与正式提交

经验法则：给机器或屏幕看，选适配图片；给打印机或人签字，选 A4 / Letter。A4 模式下图片会等比缩放放入纸面（不裁切、不变形），横图自动横放，竖图自动竖放。

边距与方向

固定纸张（A4 / Letter）下，两个参数影响成品观感：

  • 边距：无边距图片顶满纸边，打印机可能吃掉边缘内容；10mm 窄边距适合照片集；20mm 标准边距适合要装订或批注的文件。
  • 方向：「按图片自动」最省心——横图横放、竖图竖放；整份文件要统一方向时（例如打印装订）再手动固定竖版或横版。

「适配图片」模式下页面就是图片本身，边距与方向选项不生效。

画质与体积的取舍

转换器通常把图片按 JPEG 重新编码后嵌入 PDF（这是兼容性最好的做法）：

质量档典型效果适用
90–100肉眼接近无损证件、合同、扫描件（默认推荐）
75–85体积明显减小，轻微细节损失邮件附件、聊天发送
<70可见块状伪影仅草稿

体积规律：PNG 截图转 PDF 通常变小（截图大多是无损大文件）；已高度压缩的 JPG 可能略微变大，这是重编码的正常代价。对画质有硬要求的场景，用高分辨率原图 + 质量 90。

多张图片的排序技巧

PDF 的页面顺序 = 你添加图片的顺序。两个实用做法：

  1. 文件名预排序：上传前把文件重命名为 01.jpg、02.jpg、03.jpg，批量选择时天然有序（注意 1–9 补零，否则 10.jpg 会排在 2.jpg 前面）。
  2. 工具内微调：用每行的上移 / 下移按钮逐张调整，改完核对一遍缩略图顺序再生成。

隐私：云上传 vs 本地转换

主流在线转换器（iLovePDF、Smallpdf、PDF24 等）的工作方式是把你的文件上传到服务器，处理完再给你下载链接。转普通照片无所谓，但转的内容如果是证件、合同、医疗单据，就值得三思——你无法控制服务器端那份副本的留存周期。

另一条路线是纯浏览器本地转换：转换逻辑在你的浏览器里完成，文件全程不离开设备，断网也能用。本站的 图片转 PDF 工具就是这一路线——包括 PDF 文件本身都是浏览器逐字节生成的，适合证件等敏感素材。

常见问题

Q：图片转 PDF 会损失画质吗？

A：PNG 的透明通道无法保留（会铺白底），且图片通常按 JPEG 重新编码——质量 90 时肉眼几乎无损。控制体积可降到 75–85。

Q：页面尺寸选「适配图片」还是 A4？

A：屏幕上看选适配图片（每页正好一张原图）；打印或正式提交选 A4（国内/欧洲）或 Letter（北美）。

Q：把证件照片转成 PDF，上传在线工具安全吗？

A：主流工具会上传到服务器处理，证件类敏感素材不建议。改用纯浏览器本地处理的工具更稳妥。

Q：多张图片的页面顺序由什么决定？

A：由添加顺序决定。文件名按 01、02、03 预编号再批量上传，或用工具内的上移/下移按钮调整。

Q：PNG 转 PDF 和 JPG 转 PDF 有区别吗？

A：流程无区别。PNG 截图转换后通常变小；已压缩的 JPG 可能略大。透明 PNG 会被铺白底。

Q：为什么不能直接把图片改后缀叫 .pdf？

A：PDF 是有目录结构的文档格式（对象、交叉引用表、页树），不是图片格式的别名。改后缀的文件查看器打不开，必须用转换器生成合法结构。

When Images Should Become PDF

JPG / PNG are "pictures"; PDF is a "document". Convert when the recipient expects a fixed-layout file:

  • ID and document submission: government, banking, school, and visa systems accept PDF only — combine several ID photos into one file, in order.
  • Contract / receipt return: combine photographed or scanned signature pages; page order is fixed and single pages can't be swapped easily.
  • Sending many images: one PDF beats fifteen screenshots — the recipient pages through in order, and chat apps won't re-compress it.
  • Printing: placing images on A4 pages beats printing raw images — margins, centering, and scaling are all fixed.

Conversely, if the recipient needs editable source material, keep the original image format.

Page Size: Fit-to-Image vs A4 / Letter

OptionPage sizeBest for
Fit to imageEach page is exactly one imageOn-screen reading: email attachments, chat, online submission previews
A4210×297mm (595×842pt)Printing and formal submission in Europe/Asia
Letter216×279mm (612×792pt)Printing and formal submission in North America

Rule of thumb: for screens and machines, fit to image; for printers and signatures, A4 / Letter. In A4 mode images are scaled proportionally onto the paper (no cropping, no distortion), landscape images rotate the page automatically.

Margins & Orientation

For fixed paper (A4 / Letter), two parameters shape the result:

  • Margins: zero margins run images to the paper edge, where printers may clip content; 10mm narrow suits photo collections; 20mm normal suits files meant for binding or annotation.
  • Orientation: "Auto per image" is easiest — landscape images get landscape pages; fix portrait or landscape manually when a document must be uniform (e.g., for binding).

In "Fit to image" mode the page is the image itself; margin and orientation options don't apply.

Quality vs File Size

Converters typically re-encode images as JPEG before embedding (the most compatible approach):

QualityTypical resultUse
90–100Visually losslessIDs, contracts, scans (default)
75–85Clearly smaller, minor detail lossEmail attachments, chat
<70Visible blocky artifactsDrafts only

Size patterns: PNG screenshots usually shrink (lossless files encode well as JPEG); already-compressed JPGs may grow slightly — a normal cost of re-encoding. For quality-critical work, use high-resolution originals at quality 90.

Ordering Multiple Images

PDF page order = the order you add images. Two practical habits:

  1. Pre-sort by filename: rename files to 01.jpg, 02.jpg, 03.jpg before batch-selecting (zero-pad 1–9, or 10.jpg sorts before 2.jpg).
  2. Fine-tune in the tool: use the move-up / move-down buttons per row, then verify thumbnail order before generating.

Privacy: Cloud Upload vs Local Conversion

Mainstream online converters (iLovePDF, Smallpdf, PDF24, etc.) work by uploading your file to their servers and handing back a download link. For ordinary photos this doesn't matter — but for IDs, contracts, or medical bills, think twice: you don't control how long the server-side copy is retained.

The alternative is in-browser local conversion: the conversion logic runs in your browser, files never leave the device, and it works offline. Our Image to PDF tool takes this route — the PDF itself is generated byte-by-byte in your browser, suitable for sensitive material like IDs.

FAQ

Q: Does converting images to PDF lose quality?

A: PNG transparency can't survive (transparent areas get a white fill), and images are typically re-encoded as JPEG — quality 90 is visually lossless. Drop to 75–85 to shrink.

Q: Fit-to-image or A4?

A: On-screen reading → fit to image (each page is one image). Printing or formal submission → A4 (Europe/Asia) or Letter (North America).

Q: Is it safe to upload ID photos to an online converter?

A: Mainstream tools upload files to their servers. For sensitive material like IDs, prefer a tool that runs entirely in your browser.

Q: What determines the page order of multiple images?

A: The order you add them. Pre-number filenames 01, 02, 03 before batch upload, or reorder with move-up/move-down buttons.

Q: PNG to PDF vs JPG to PDF — any difference?

A: Same workflow. PNG screenshots usually shrink; compressed JPGs may grow slightly. Transparent PNGs get a white fill.

Q: Why can't I just rename an image to .pdf?

A: PDF is a structured document format (objects, cross-reference tables, page tree), not an image extension. Renamed files won't open — a real converter must generate valid structure.
